title: unstable_prefetch
description: API Reference for the unstable_prefetch function, which keeps a subtree out of a route's App Shell so it renders on a per-link prefetch or a navigation.
version: experimental

Calling `await unstable_prefetch()` defers the code below it to a per-link prefetch or a navigation, instead of rendering it in the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary takes its place in the shell, and the deferred content renders once one of those happens.

It is meant to defer content that the App Shell would otherwise render, typically content that depends on session data and is expensive to generate. During a build-time prerender nothing is deferred, so content below `unstable_prefetch()` is prerendered as usual.

## Usage

00060|

The `prefetch` route segment config controls how a segment is prefetched during client-side navigation. By default, the framework manages the strategy based on the app's [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) setting. >
> - The `prefetch` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
> - `prefetch` cannot be used when the segment is a Client Component.
> - The meaningful values to set are `'partial'` and `'force-disabled'`. `'auto'` is the default and is equivalent to omitting the export; don't write `prefetch = 'auto'` explicitly.

---
title: Ensuring instant navigations
description: Learn how to structure your app to prefetch and prerender more content, providing instant page loads and client navigations.
nav_title: Instant navigation
related:
  title: Learn more
  description: Explore the full instant API, caching, and revalidation.
  links:
    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant

    - app/getting-started/caching
    - app/getting-started/revalidating
    - app/guides/prefetching
---

This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.

## What "instant" means

A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.

00245| // After - the lookup is cached behind the session value
00246| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00247| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
00248| 
00249| async function getTopics(team) {
00250|   'use cache'
00251|   return db.topics.forTeam(team)
00252| }
00253| 
00254| async function TeamTopics() {
00255|   const team = (await cookies()).get('team')?.value
00256|   return <TopicList topics={await getTopics(team)} />
00257| }
00258| 
00259| export default function Page() {
00260|   return (
00261|     <Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}>
00262|       <TeamTopics />
00263|     </Suspense>
00264|   )
00265| }
00266| ```
00267| 
00268| ### URL data
00269| 
00270| [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
00271| 
00272| ### Real-time content
00273| 
00274| A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
00275| 
00276| | Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
00277| | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00278| | [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
00279| | [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
00280| | [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
00281| | [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
00282| | [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |
00283| 
00284| ## Adopting incrementally
00285| 
00286| Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.
00287| 
00288| Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. Navigating through one of these links in development surfaces the [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight, naming the destination and pointing at its fixes:
00289| 
00290| <FixCardGrid>
00291|   <FixCard
00292|     group="upgrade"
00293|     title="Opt into Partial Prefetching"
00294|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#opt-into-partial-prefetching"
00295|     snippets={[
00296|       { text: '// page.tsx or layout.tsx' },
00297|       { text: "export const prefetch = 'partial'", highlight: true },
00298|     ]}
00299|   />
00300|   <FixCard
00301|     group="disable"
00302|     title="Use the default prefetch"
00303|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#use-the-default-prefetch"
00304|     snippets={[
00305|       { text: '<Link href="/dashboard">', highlight: true },
00306|       { text: '  Dashboard' },
00307|       { text: '</Link>' },
00308|     ]}
00309|   />
00310| </FixCardGrid>
00311| 
00312| Each card is clickable and opens a page with patterns, code samples, and trade-offs.
00313| 
00314| 1. Start with one destination. Preserve the intended prefetched UI and update its `prefetch={true}` links using the [patterns above](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches). Then add `export const prefetch = 'partial'` to its page or layout, which clears the insight for every link pointing at the route:
00315| 
00316|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00317|    // Before
00318|    export default function Page() {
00319|      return <Dashboard />
00320|    }
00321|    ```
00322| 
00323|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00324|    // Before
00325|    export default function Page() {
00326|      return <Dashboard />
00327|    }
00328|    ```
00329| 
00330|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00331|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00332|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00333| 
00334|    export default function Page() {
00335|      return <Dashboard />
00336|    }
00337|    ```
00338| 
00339|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00340|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00341|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00342| 
00343|    export default function Page() {
00344|      return <Dashboard />
00345|    }
00346|    ```
00347| 
00348| 2. Deploy the change. Links to the adopted destination load the App Shell, and the insight keeps surfacing for the destinations you haven't reached.
00349| 3. Repeat until every destination in scope is adopted, then [enable the flag](#enable-partial-prefetching).
00350| 
00351| The per-route `prefetch = 'partial'` exports are now redundant. Remove them in one pass with the [`remove-partial-prefetch`](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#remove-partial-prefetch) codemod, which strips `export const prefetch = 'partial'` from every `page` and `layout`:
00352| 
00353| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00354| npx @next/codemod@canary remove-partial-prefetch ./app
00355| ```
00356| 
00357| > **Good to know**: Pass `./src/app` in a `src/` project. A wrong path reports `0 ok` instead of failing, so check the file count.
00358| 
00359| The codemod removes only the `'partial'` value and leaves other values such as `prefetch = 'force-disabled'` in place.
00360| 
00361| ## Move URL data behind Suspense
00362| 
00363| With the flag enabled, Next.js validates each App Shell as you navigate in development. The App Shell is shared across every link to a route, so it can't contain data that belongs to a single URL. Reading [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional) or [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) outside a [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary ties the shell to the link's URL and surfaces the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight, naming the route and pointing at its fixes:
00364| 
00365| <FixCardGrid>
00366|   <FixCard
00367|     group="stream"
00368|     title="Wrap in or move into Suspense"
00369|     href="/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data#wrap-in-or-move-into-suspense"
00370|     snippets={[
00371|       { text: '<Suspense fallback={…}>', highlight: true },
00372|       { text: '  <Details params={params} />' },
00373|       { text: '</Suspense>', highlight: true },
00374|     ]}
00375|   />
00376|   <FixCard
00377|     group="block"
00378|     title="Allow blocking route"
00379|     href="/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data#allow-blocking-route"
00380|     snippets={[
00381|       { text: '// page.tsx or layout.tsx' },
00382|       { text: 'export const instant = false', highlight: true },
00383|     ]}
00384|   />

00387| The insight never blocks the build, so this pass can happen any time after the flag is on. Load every route in `next dev` to check for it.

00391| ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher

00393| export default async function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>) {
00394|   const { slug } = await params
00395|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00396|   return (
00397|     <ProductLayout>
00398|       <Details product={product} />
00399|     </ProductLayout>
00400|   )
00401| }
00402| ```
00403| 
00404| ```jsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.js" switcher

00407|   const { slug } = await params
00408|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00409|   return (
00410|     <ProductLayout>
00411|       <Details product={product} />
00412|     </ProductLayout>
00413|   )
00414| }
00415| ```
00416| 
00417| ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00418| // After - pass the promise down without awaiting it
00419| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00420| import { ProductDetails } from './product-details'
00421| 
00422| export default function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>) {
00423|   return (
00424|     <ProductLayout>
00425|       <Suspense fallback={<DetailsSkeleton />}>
00426|         <ProductDetails params={params} />
00427|       </Suspense>
00428|     </ProductLayout>
00429|   )
00430| }
00431| ```
00432| 
00433| ```jsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00434| // After - pass the promise down without awaiting it
00435| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00436| import { ProductDetails } from './product-details'
00437| 
00438| export default function Page({ params }) {
00439|   return (
00440|     <ProductLayout>
00441|       <Suspense fallback={<DetailsSkeleton />}>
00442|         <ProductDetails params={params} />
00443|       </Suspense>
00444|     </ProductLayout>
00445|   )
00446| }
00447| ```
00448| 
00449| The child awaits the promise inside the boundary:
00450| 
00451| ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/product-details.tsx" switcher
00452| export async function ProductDetails({
00453|   params,
00454| }: Pick<PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>, 'params'>) {
00455|   const { slug } = await params
00456|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00457|   return <Details product={product} />
00458| }
00459| ```
00460|

00473| ## Prefetching URL data
00474| 
00475| Content that depends on [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) can't be included in the shared App Shell, so it streams in after navigation. ---
title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
nav_title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
description: Learn how to enable Partial Prefetching and what changes for `<Link>`.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn more about prefetching and instant navigations.
  links:
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch
    - app/api-reference/functions/prefetch
    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
---

[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

part.text:
Configured the application to keep related products out of the default product page prefetch while having them immediately available when navigating from the featured-product link:

1. **Enabled Partial Prefetching** in `next.config.ts` (`partialPrefetching: true`) alongside `cacheComponents: true`.
2. **Deferred related products** in `app/product/page.tsx` by moving the related products section into an async component wrapped in React `<Suspense>`, awaiting `unstable_prefetch()` from `next/cache` prior to retrieving the cached products data.
3. **Opted into per-link prefetching** on the featured product link in `app/page.tsx` with `<Link href="/product" prefetch={true}>`.
